messages:
alice: Quick heads-up — we got a SAR (subject request) for user alice@example.com. Erase API returned 200 for main DB, but OS snapshots in eu-west still reference the old KMS key. Audit log shows a gap around the rotation window. Can we triage?
raj: ugh. Which rotation? the emergency rotate last month?
maria: I see the SAR in the tracker. Snapshot IDs: snap-0a1b2c3d, snap-0f4e5d6c. Both encrypted with alias/redwood-kms-old.
julian: @raj that was the targeted rotate for compromised key material (2025-11-12). We did a staged rotate with fallback for live volumes only — snapshots were left as-is to avoid breakage.
alice: Right — the erase job only touches the DB+live blobstore. Backups/snapshots are separate. Legal wants evidence of deletion for the SAR; they asked for proof-of-deletion and timeline.
kate-legal: We need a defendable artifact: list of actions, what was purged, dates, and whether any residual ciphertext remains in backups. If backup snapshots still reference old key, we need either a re-encrypt-and-delete or an attestation describing risk.
raj: Technical Q: can we decrypt those snapshots to scrub? We don't have cross-account decryption keys for the old keystore in eu-west.
maria: Snapshots are region-bound. Our infra account holds them; the KMS alias was rotated but old key material is scheduled for destruction next week. If we destroy old key, those snapshots become unreadable (which helps privacy but complicates forensics).
julian: Ops perspective: destructive key deletion counts as data destruction but also prevents us from proving contents later. Legal: what do you want — proof of deletion now, or preserve for potential dispute?
kate-legal: Preferably proof for the SAR. If destroying key makes the snapshot irrecoverable, we can use that as evidence but need notarized logs showing key schedule and access control at time of SAR.
alice: There's also an audit gap: our KMS access logs in that window (2025-11-11 23:00 -> 2025-11-12 02:00 UTC) show missing CloudTrail entries due to a log-forwarder outage. That weakens the notarization.
raj: Great. So we have three issues: (1) residual ciphertext in snapshots, (2) old key scheduled to be destroyed, (3) missing audit entries.
maria: Proposed mitigation: 1) Snapshot quarantine: tag and isolate copies into a restricted bucket; 2) Run a targeted re-encrypt using a temp-rotate-key we control, so we can then run a safe purge path; 3) Reconstruct audit evidence from node-level syslogs and s3 access logs where possible.
julian: Re-encrypting snapshots in-region requires snapshot export flow — I can script an export -> re-encrypt -> import, estimate ~2 hours for the two snapshots (small, ~30GB each). Risk: brief snapshot downtime and ops privileges.
raj: Who has the AWS perms? I need a breakglass service-account or we use the erasure-runner role? Prefer minimal blast radius.
alice: Use erasure-runner with a timebound session and recorded session logs. I'll open the ephemeral IAM session and attach an approval from @kate-legal in thread.
kate-legal: Approve the ephemeral session for re-encrypt and deletion for these snapshot IDs. Please capture all commands and timestamps.
ops-bot: deploy:erasure-runner session started by alice at 2025-11-17T16:12:05Z (session-id: sess-9f8e7d).
raj: OK starting script:```
aws ec2 copy-snapshot --source-region eu-west-1 --source-snapshot-id snap-0a1b2c3d --kms-key-id alias/redwood-kms-temp --description "re-encrypt for SAR" ```
maria: Make sure to set --presigned-url timeout and to tag copies with sar:case=USR-2025-114.
julian: Also capture the snapshot manifest and include the pre/post kms-key id in the artifact store (/legal-proofs/sar/USR-2025-114/).
alice: After re-encrypt+verify, we will run the erase pipeline against the re-encrypted snapshot and then destroy the temp key. Document everything.
kate-legal: If the audit gap prevents us from fully reconstructing who initiated the rotate originally, we need a mitigation memo signed by security + ops describing the intended rotate and risk assessment. That plus the snapshot re-encrypt+deletion artifacts should suffice for the SAR response.
raj: One more thing — RBAC change request. The erasure-runner role increase we need for snapshot copy requires an sts:AssumeRole addition for erasure-runner -> backup-admin. I can open PR but wanted to check approvals.
maria: Keep it scoped to action:ec2:CopySnapshot, ec2:DeleteSnapshot, kms:Encrypt, kms:ReEncrypt, kms:ScheduleKeyDeletion. Timebound to 2 hours.
julian: I'll pair with @raj on the script run. Plan: 1) snapshot copy -> temp key; 2) verify checksum; 3) run erase pipeline; 4) delete temp key; 5) push artifacts to legal.
alice: Action owners: raj (run), julian (ops assist), maria (artifact collector), alice (coord + session control), kate-legal (accept artifact). Timeline: start within 4 hours, finish EOD if no issues.
kate-legal: Confirmed — legal will prepare SAR letter and accept artifact chain. Keep me posted.
raj: Kickoff in 10m. I'll post progress updates here. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: snapshot-copy job queued (job-id: jc-3321)
alice: Note for runbook: we should add a 'snapshot erase' step to DSAR checklist and flag snapshots older than retention-window for periodic review. Filing backlog ticket.
maria: Filing infra ticket INFRA-2025-998: add snapshot-scrub step + reporter: maria.
julian: If anything blocks, escalate to sec-oncall.
raj: update: copy succeeded for snap-0a1b2c3d, verifying checksum...
alice: thanks team, keep logs and include raw aws CLI output in the artifact bundle (redacted for creds).
kate-legal: once bundle is ready, upload to /legal-wg/sar-evidence/ and ping me. We'll close SAR within 10 business days.
raj: done for first snapshot, proceeding to second.
ops-bot: snapshot-copy job completed (jc-3321)
alice: last check — ensure we also snapshot the IAM policy change PR and the session approver logs for paper trail.
maria: will include PR diff link and session recording.
julian: moving to cleanup now, will post final artifact link when done.
alice: closing loop: after this, create a small postmortem for the log-forwarder outage and remediate the CloudTrail pipeline.
kate-legal: thanks all — this workflow looks defensible.
raj: final artifact uploaded: s3://legal-proofs/sar/USR-2025-114/artifact-bundle.tar.gz (contains manifest, CLI logs, snapshot-manifests, PR diffs, session-recording).
alice: great job. I'll file the follow-ups and update the DSAR playbook.
